reason: The thermochemistry, ideal-gas calculation, exact raw value, and three-significant-figure rounding are correct and formally verified. However, the source prints Q = 2.2×10^5 m^3 without a time denominator, so it does not uniquely determine energy per day. The candidate correctly discloses this omission, conditions 7.03×10^12 J day^-1 on a one-day volume basis, and proves that different time bases give different daily energies.

coverage.evidence: The exact derivation gives ΔrH298 = -802.3 kJ mol^-1, ΔrCp = 12 J mol^-1 K^-1, ΔrH2000 = -781.876 kJ mol^-1, n = 5572875000000/619393 mol, and Eraw = 4357297213500000000/619393 = 7.03478601388779×10^12 J. This rounds correctly to 7.03×10^12 at a 10^10-J quantum. The numerical daily value applies only when the printed volume is interpreted as one day's flow.

unsupported_assumptions: The boxed numerical result assumes that the printed 2.2×10^5 m^3 is the methane volume delivered in exactly one day; neither the question page nor the blank answer sheet supplies that time basis.
